skills.name: search-first
skills.title: Research before implementation
skills.description: Research existing project code, primary framework documentation and maintained packages before adding a feature, utility, dependency or integration.
adaptations: Search the repository with `rg` first, then read the relevant architecture, neighboring implementations and tests.
Check primary .NET, EF Core, Vue, Vuetify and package documentation using available tools. State which searches were unavailable.
Use the PWA's `packageManager` field and pnpm; search NuGet for .NET dependencies. Prefer existing helpers over adding a package.
Keep research proportional to the change. Use the existing project skills before looking for another agent or external service.
Reuse the authorized task scope and known requirements; continue routine research and reversible implementation without requesting redundant approval.

skills.name: tdd-workflow
skills.title: Behavior-focused testing
skills.description: Use when changing project behavior or fixing a regression to run the failing-test, minimal-fix and refactor cycle. Owns the cross-stack testing process; C# fixture/assertion details belong to ecc-csharp-testing.
adaptations: Use xUnit for the .NET projects and the configured Vitest script for the PWA; inspect nearby tests before choosing fixtures or assertions.
For a bug, run a regression test that fails for the intended reason, make the smallest fix and rerun that same test before refactoring.
Do not run ECC's package-manager detector or install sample Jest, React, Bun or coverage tooling. The project already specifies its runners.
Keep tests focused on user-visible behavior and meaningful boundaries; instruction-only edits do not require synthetic application tests.
The full suite in AGENTS.md remains required. Use existing coverage configuration; do not add an arbitrary 80% threshold or new evidence-report directory.
Record actual RED/GREEN results and any unverified checks in the PR body. Routine test commands within the authorized task do not need repeated approval.

skills.name: security-review
skills.title: Security and data isolation
skills.description: Review the project's authentication, authorization, personal data, uploads, webhooks and integrations for cross-user access and sensitive-data exposure.
adaptations: Read `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/security-configuration.md` and the relevant API documentation. Preserve the existing authentication and authorization boundaries.
Treat route ids, headers and request bodies as untrusted until verified. Keep visibility and redaction decisions in logic, not in controllers.
Test denied access, missing permissions and response redaction when those boundaries change.
Use parameterized EF Core/Npgsql access, input validation, signature verification for webhooks and rate limiting where they exist.
Keep secrets in the configured secret stores/environment, redact credentials and personal data from logs, and avoid printing secret matches.
Apply relevant checklist items to the project's actual stack. Do not switch token storage, add Supabase/RLS, introduce blockchain tooling or run automatic dependency upgrades from upstream examples.

skills.name: dotnet-patterns
skills.title: .NET architecture and implementation
skills.description: Use when writing or reviewing C# logic, services, dependency injection, async work and EF Core access in the project's ASP.NET Core solution.
adaptations: Read `docs/architecture.md` and .editorconfig. Preserve Starter.WebApi controllers, Starter logic/services, Starter.Abstractions contracts and Starter.Persistence entities.
Place each service/logic interface in its own file in Starter.Abstractions. Interface methods return models and do not accept HttpContext.
Use `IHttpContextAccessor` where implementations need the request; keep authorization-sensitive visibility decisions in logic.
Preserve the project's domain exceptions and ApiResponse/problem-details behavior rather than introducing an unrelated Result type, repository layer or Minimal API rewrite.
Use async operations and cancellation where supported. Never run parallel EF operations on the same StarterContext instance.
Follow existing model mutability and mappings; do not convert tracked EF entities to immutable records merely to follow an example.

skills.name: csharp-testing
skills.title: C# unit and database testing
skills.description: Use when implementing or reviewing .NET test code in the project: xUnit fixtures, mocks, assertions, ASP.NET integration tests and PostgreSQL regression tests. The RED/GREEN process belongs to ecc-tdd-workflow.
adaptations: Inspect existing tests and project references in Starter.WebApi.UnitTests and Starter.WebApi.PostgresTests; reuse their fixtures and installed assertion/mocking libraries.
Put behavior-focused unit tests in the existing .NET test project. Cover success, invalid input, denied access and missing records as relevant.
Use Starter.WebApi.PostgresTests for provider-specific translation, constraints, migrations and concurrency; in-memory EF cannot prove PostgreSQL behavior.

Run `dotnet test Starter.sln` for the required solution suite. The PostgreSQL project is outside the solution and additionally runs with `dotnet test Starter.WebApi.PostgresTests` when database behavior changes and Docker is available.
Do not install FluentAssertions, NSubstitute, Bogus or a new test framework solely because upstream examples use them. State unavailable database infrastructure and unrun checks.

skills.name: vue-patterns
skills.title: Vue and Vuetify implementation
skills.description: Use when changing reactive application logic in the project's Vue PWA: composables, Pinia, routing, request lifecycle, stale responses and frontend tests. Visual components, branding, layout and Material Design belong to material-design.
adaptations: Use Vue 3, TypeScript, Vuetify, Pinia and the existing Vite layout. Read the canonical `material-design` skill; this is not a Nuxt application.
Use the existing `useLoader` and `useAsyncAction` helpers in Starter.PWA as required by AGENTS.md, with Vuetify skeletons for content loading.
Use the existing API wrapper and generated client; never hand-edit src/logic/api.ts or replace the API lifecycle with sample fetch helpers.
Preserve current store/component conventions and the English/Dutch translations; avoid unrelated folder or store rewrites.
Use configured Vitest tests and the canonical `webapp-testing` skill for browser checks at phone and desktop widths. Run the PWA's required pnpm checks.

skills.name: database-migrations
skills.title: EF Core migration planning
skills.description: Use when changing the project's EF Core entities, schema, constraints, indexes or data migrations to plan compatibility and validate PostgreSQL behavior.
adaptations: The project uses EF Core with PostgreSQL. Inspect StarterContext, existing migrations and affected mappings before editing.
Use EF migrations in the Starter project with Starter.WebApi as the startup project. Review generated SQL and the model snapshot.
Plan rollout compatibility, data backfill, nullability, defaults, index locking and recovery for each schema change; prefer small additive steps when appropriate.
Use a disposable local/test database for validation. An application code task does not authorize applying a migration to a production or shared remote database.
Validate affected queries and constraints with Starter.WebApi.PostgresTests when Docker is available, and run the full required solution/PWA suite.
Treat Prisma, Django, Alembic and standalone production SQL examples as reference material; keep the EF Core migration mechanism.

skills.name: postgres-patterns
skills.title: PostgreSQL query performance
skills.description: Use when investigating or changing the project's PostgreSQL queries, EF Core projections, indexes, pagination, constraints or database performance.
adaptations: Trace the EF Core/Npgsql query from logic to StarterContext and inspect its generated SQL before proposing an index or raw query.
Keep visibility filters intact; select only fields needed by the response and preserve stable ordering for pagination.
Use a disposable test database for EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE and query experiments. Do not run mutating plans or migrations on shared production data.
Add indexes through an EF Core migration, examine write/locking costs and verify provider-specific behavior in Starter.WebApi.PostgresTests.
Keep existing identifiers and schema conventions. Do not introduce Supabase, change PostgreSQL settings globally or add RLS policies just to copy the upstream examples.
